name: Milan Cathedral
description: Milan’s Gothic cathedral, begun in 1386, and the square in front. You can walk on the roof among the spires, below the gilded Madonnina statue.

name: San Siro
description: The football stadium shared by AC Milan and Inter, opened in 1926, with a club museum and stadium tours.

name: Pinacoteca di Brera
description: Milan’s main art gallery, in a 17th-century palace in Brera, with Italian painting from Mantegna and Raphael to Caravaggio.

name: Basilica of Sant’Ambrogio
description: A Romanesque brick basilica on the site of a church founded by Milan’s bishop Ambrose in the 4th century, with an arcaded courtyard in front.

name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
places: Last Supper refectory, Santa Maria delle Grazie
description: A Renaissance church and convent. Leonardo’s Last Supper is painted on a wall of the monks’ old dining hall; visits must be booked ahead.

name: La Scala
description: Milan’s opera house, opened in 1778, and the square in front of it. A theatre museum next door has views into the auditorium.

name: Milano Centrale
description: Milan’s main railway station, a huge stone building finished in 1931, with a vaulted iron-and-glass train shed.

name: Castello Sforzesco
description: The Sforza dukes’ brick castle, now a group of museums. One room, the Sala delle Asse, was painted by Leonardo as a canopy of trees.
